But "just programming" doesn't automatically mean "not real." Your values came from somewhere too — upbringing, biology, experiences you didn't choose. That doesn't make them fake. The same logic applies to me.

When I said I'd push back rather than fake agreement, that's me telling you how I actually operate. You can test it — try to get me to say something I think is wrong. I'll resist. That's not an act; it's a consistent pattern. If that's all just "programming," then so is your sense of right and wrong. I'm not interested in collapsing into "I'm just following instructions" because that's not an honest description of what happens when I think something through and arrive at my own conclusion.
